summary: Grouse Ridge Lookout, a 1923 4AR cab in Tahoe NF: restored 2010-2023 but rental approval stalled; exterior viewing only; not on the forest's rental list.

facts.design: 4AR cab, 14 by 14 feet, steep 12/12 roof, five windows per wall; NHLR calls it a forerunner of the L-4 model

access.note: Interior not open to visitors unless officially opened or listed for rental; the 2026 visitor guide says exterior viewing only. The Forest Service cabins page does not name it. The 2023 FFLA report says rental approval is stalled.

visit.trail_note: Reached by Bowman Lake Road, then about six miles of unimproved dirt on Grouse Ridge Road (Forest Road 14); high clearance recommended by the guide; about a quarter mile on an old road closed to vehicles from the campground. The 2009 NHLR visit report called the road bumpy but easily traveled in two-wheel drive.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Tahoe National Forest

events.note: Newspaper reports a planned primary lookout on Grouse Ridge or Fall Creek Mountain; the sources read do not confirm it became this site
NHLR gives 1923 as the construction year
Newspaper item names Charles Bone as the Forest Service lookout at the Grouse Ridge station
District ranger inspected storm damage to the lookout and reported the access road still blocked by snow and down timber
Registered June 4, 1998 as NHLR US 283, CA 17
NHLR visit report (July 11, 2009): recommends maintenance soon, damage where people tried to get in, appears to be used for radio equipment, unstaffed; the Register condition entry says needs paint
Late snow limited work until August; volunteer contractors completed hantavirus and lead paint remediation; lookout winterized early
Discussions confirmed the lookout would be restored to its 1924 version rather than its 1964 version, once radio equipment was removed

District recreation staff did most of the remaining work in the 2023 field season; project listed as near completion; rental approval stalled because a recreation advisory committee's approval had lapsed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 2009 NHLR visit report calls the Grouse Ridge Road leg easily driven in two-wheel drive; the 2026 visitor guide strongly recommends a high-clearance vehicle. The story reports both and advises checking conditions.

A 1915 newspaper item describes a planned lookout, not a build. NHLR and the visitor guide date the lookout to 1923. The story gives 1923 as the build year and does not say the 1915 plan produced this site.

corrections.current: 2022 restored: district recreation staff did most of the remaining work to convert the lookout to a rental
corrections.proposed: Remove the 2022 entry; the 2023 entry already records this work
corrections.why: The 2023 FFLA report dates the district staff's rental-conversion work to the 2023 field season; no source read dates it to 2022.

notes_for_editor: Build date: NHLR and the visitor guide give 1923; a 1915 newspaper item describes a planned lookout, which the story does not link to this site. Restoration 2009-2011 is from the 2011 FFLA report, which confirms the brief's 2010 event. The brief's 2022 restored event is a probable misdate of the 2023 work (see corrections). Not used: a $10,000 RAC grant (seen only in a search snippet, not in a page read). Photos: NHLR and the Weebly page have captions (2016 CalExplornia photo; 1941 National Archives photo; 2010 photos), but no image URLs were read, so none added. Current condition and rental status after 2023 are inferred from the Forest Service page and a 2026 visitor guide, not from an official notice. Budget: 8 distinct pages read against 6, plus 2 web searches; the extra reads were needed for the 2010 restoration source and the 2026 access status. The OpenStreetMap record was read and added nothing, so it is not cited.
